fullPassage: The Industrial Revolution did more than just invent new materials or machines. It invented a new process for manufacturing: the modern factory. Prior to around 1850, most piano shops used an apprentice system in which a master builder taught younger workers the skills of the trade, usually over the course of many years. The larger piano shops did have specialists—for example, one person who specialized in soundboards, another who made hammers, and so on. But even the largest piano makers of that time produced no more than 5-10 pianos per year per worker, as pianos were still made essentially one at a time. The development of a true piano factory occurring first in the United States, led by Jonas Chickering in Boston and later the Steinway family in New York City. These factories led to improvements in both efficiency and quality. For example, one of the factories of the time had its own iron casting facility where it made its metal plates, which were thought to be the best available.

questions.passage: The Industrial Revolution did more than just (A)[invent / destroy] new materials or machines. It invented a new process for (B)[manufacturing / recycling]: the modern factory. Prior to around 1850, most piano shops used an (C)[apprentice / automated] system in which a master builder taught younger workers the skills of the trade.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 산업혁명은 새 재료를 발명(invent)하고, 제조(manufacturing)의 새 과정을 만들었다. 대부분의 피아노 공방은 도제(apprentice) 시스템을 사용했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② invent — manufacturing — apprentice: 원문과 일치
❌ ① destroy(파괴하다): invent의 반의어
❌ ③ recycling(재활용): manufacturing과 다른 의미
❌ ④ automated(자동화된): apprentice와 다른 의미
det.tip: invent = 발명하다, manufacturing = 제조, apprentice = 도제/견습

questions.passage: The larger piano shops did have (A)[specialists / amateurs]—for example, one person who specialized in soundboards, another who made hammers. But even the largest piano makers of that time produced no more than 5-10 pianos per year per worker, as pianos were still made (B)[essentially / rarely] one at a time. These factories led to (C)[improvements / setbacks] in both efficiency and quality.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 큰 공방에는 전문가(specialists)가 있었다. 피아노는 본질적으로(essentially) 하나씩 만들어졌다. 공장은 개선(improvements)으로 이어졌다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① specialists — essentially — improvements: 원문과 일치
❌ ② amateurs(아마추어): specialists의 반의어
❌ ③ rarely(거의 ~않은): essentially와 다른 의미
❌ ④ setbacks(후퇴): improvements의 반의어
det.tip: specialist = 전문가, essentially = 본질적으로, improvement = 개선/향상

questions.passage: The development of a true piano factory (A)[occurred / vanished] first in the United States, led by Jonas Chickering in Boston and later the Steinway family in New York City. These factories led to improvements in both (B)[efficiency / inefficiency] and quality. For example, one of the factories of the time had its own iron (C)[casting / painting] facility.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 진정한 피아노 공장은 미국에서 처음 발생(occurred)했다. 공장은 효율성(efficiency)과 품질의 개선으로 이어졌다. 자체 철 주조(casting) 시설이 있었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ occurred — efficiency — casting: 원문과 일치
❌ ① vanished(사라졌다): occurred의 반의어
❌ ② inefficiency(비효율): efficiency의 반의어
❌ ④ painting(도색): casting과 다른 의미
det.tip: occur = 발생하다, efficiency = 효율성, casting = 주조

questions.passage: The Industrial Revolution did more than just invent new materials or machines. It invented a new process for manufacturing: the modern factory. Prior to around 1850, most piano shops used an ①<u>apprentice</u> system in which a master builder ②<u>taught</u> younger workers the skills of the trade, usually over the course of many years. The larger piano shops did have ③<u>beginners</u>—for example, one person who specialized in soundboards, another who made ④<u>hammers</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ beginners(초보자) → specialists(전문가): 방음판이나 해머를 전문으로 만드는 사람은 '전문가'이므로 beginners는 부적절.
det.analysis:
✅ ① apprentice(도제): 원문 일치
✅ ② taught(가르쳤다): 원문 일치
❌ ③ beginners(초보자) → specialists(전문가): 반의어로 교체됨
✅ ④ hammers(해머): 원문 일치
det.tip: specialist(전문가) ↔ beginner(초보자) — specialized in = ~을 전문으로 하다

questions.passage: But even the largest piano makers of that time produced no more than 5-10 pianos per year per worker, as pianos were still made essentially one at a time. The development of a true piano factory occurred first in the United States. These factories led to ①<u>improvements</u> in both efficiency and ②<u>quality</u>. For example, one of the factories of the time had its own iron casting ③<u>facility</u> where it made its metal plates, which were thought to be the ④<u>worst</u> available.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ worst(최악의) → best(최고의): 금속판은 '최고의' 것으로 여겨졌으므로 worst는 부적절.
det.analysis:
✅ ① improvements(개선): 원문 일치
✅ ② quality(품질): 원문 일치
✅ ③ facility(시설): 원문 일치
❌ ④ worst(최악의) → best(최고의): 반의어로 교체됨
det.tip: best(최고의) ↔ worst(최악의)

questions.passage: The Industrial Revolution did more than just invent new materials or machines. It invented a new process for __________: the modern factory.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 산업혁명은 제조(manufacturing)의 새로운 과정을 발명했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ manufacturing(제조): 원문과 일치
❌ ① transportation(운송): 문맥과 맞지 않음
❌ ② communication(통신): 문맥과 맞지 않음
❌ ④ agriculture(농업): 문맥과 맞지 않음
det.tip: manufacturing = 제조, 생산 | the modern factory와 직접 연결

questions.passage: Prior to around 1850, most piano shops used an apprentice system in which a master builder taught younger workers the skills of the __________, usually over the course of many years.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 도제 시스템에서 장인이 젊은 노동자에게 직업(trade)의 기술을 가르쳤다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ trade(직업): 원문과 일치, the skills of the trade = 직업 기술
❌ ① sword(칼): 문맥과 맞지 않음
❌ ② piano(피아노): 너무 좁은 의미
❌ ③ revolution(혁명): 문맥과 맞지 않음
det.tip: trade = 직업, 거래 | the skills of the trade = 직업적 기술/노하우

questions.passage: These factories led to improvements in both efficiency and quality. For example, one of the factories of the time had its own iron casting __________ where it made its metal plates.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 공장은 자체 철 주조 시설(facility)을 갖추고 있었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② facility(시설): 원문과 일치
❌ ① vehicle(차량): 문맥과 맞지 않음
❌ ③ costume(의상): 문맥과 맞지 않음
❌ ④ document(문서): 문맥과 맞지 않음
det.tip: facility = 시설, 설비 | iron casting facility = 철 주조 시설

questions.passage: Prior to around 1850, most piano shops used an <u>apprentice</u> system in which a master builder taught younger workers.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 apprentice의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: apprentice = 도제/견습생, trainee = 수련생 → 동의어
det.analysis:
✅ ① trainee(수련생): apprentice의 동의어
❌ ② expert(전문가): 반대 개념
❌ ③ employer(고용주): 다른 의미
❌ ④ inventor(발명가): 다른 의미
det.tip: apprentice = trainee = 도제, 견습생 | 기술을 배우는 초보자

questions.passage: These factories led to <u>improvements</u> in both efficiency and quality.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 improvements의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: improvements = 개선, advances = 발전 → 동의어
det.analysis:
✅ ③ advances(발전): improvements의 동의어
❌ ① declines(감소): 반의어
❌ ② failures(실패): 반의어
❌ ④ problems(문제): 반의어
det.tip: improvement = advance = progress = enhancement = 개선, 발전

questions.passage: The larger piano shops did have specialists—for example, one person who <u>specialized</u> in soundboards.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 specialized의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: specialized = 전문화했다, focused = 집중했다 → 동의어
det.analysis:
✅ ④ focused(집중했다): specialized의 유사어
❌ ① competed(경쟁했다): 다른 의미
❌ ② struggled(고군분투했다): 다른 의미
❌ ③ disappeared(사라졌다): 다른 의미
det.tip: specialize in = focus on = concentrate on = ~을 전문으로 하다

questions.passage: These factories led to improvements in both <u>efficiency</u> and quality.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 efficiency의 의미와 가장 먼 것은?

det.korean: efficiency = 효율성 ↔ wastefulness = 낭비
det.analysis:
❌ ② wastefulness(낭비): efficiency의 반의어 → 가장 먼 의미
✅ ① productivity(생산성): 유사어
✅ ③ effectiveness(효과성): 유사어
✅ ④ competence(능력): 유사어
det.tip: efficiency(효율성) = productivity ↔ wastefulness(낭비) = inefficiency(비효율)

questions.passage: But even the <u>largest</u> piano makers of that time produced no more than 5-10 pianos per year per worker.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 largest의 의미와 가장 먼 것은?

det.korean: largest = 가장 큰 ↔ smallest = 가장 작은
det.analysis:
❌ ④ smallest(가장 작은): largest의 반의어 → 가장 먼 의미
✅ ① biggest(가장 큰): 동의어
✅ ② greatest(가장 큰): 유사어
✅ ③ most major(가장 주요한): 유사어
det.tip: largest = biggest = greatest ↔ smallest = tiniest

questions.passage: Prior to around 1850, most piano shops used an apprentice system in which a master builder taught younger workers the skills of the <u>trade</u>, usually over the course of many years.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 trade가 이 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: trade는 다의어: ① 무역/교역 ② 직업/기술직. 이 문맥에서는 '직업, 기술직(a skilled job)'의 의미.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ a skilled job or craft(기술직): the skills of the trade = 직업 기술
❌ ① buying and selling goods(상품 매매): 무역의 의미이나 문맥과 맞지 않음
❌ ② an exchange of items(물물교환): 문맥과 맞지 않음
❌ ④ a business agreement(사업 계약): 문맥과 맞지 않음
det.tip: trade는 다의어: ① 무역(international trade) ② 직업(learn a trade) ③ 교환(trade gifts)

"a person who is learning a trade from a skilled employer, having agreed to work for a fixed period"

det.analysis:

❌ ③ specialist(전문가): 이미 숙련된 사람
❌ ④ inventor(발명가): 다른 의미
det.tip: apprentice = 도제, 견습생 | 기술을 배우는 과정에 있는 사람

det.analysis:

questions.passage: The larger piano shops did have specialists—for example, one person who specialized in soundboards, another who made hammers.
questions.stem:

det.tip: special(특별한, 형용사) → specialize(전문화하다, 동사) → specialization(전문화, 명사)
